title: Guaranteed throughput bid prep notes
content:
Purpose:
Prep notes for AE/SE when responding to RFPs or RFIs that ask for guaranteed/committed throughput for dedicated inference capacity. This is a working playbook — keep responses concise and procurement-ready. Aim: accelerate procurement, reduce back-and-forth on measurement windows, and limit legal drift on SLO credit language.

Top-level positioning (one-liner):
Offer a reserved GPU pool with measurable throughput and isolation guarantees — backed by observability, automatic fallback policies, and a transparent credit model so buyers get predictable inference economics without operational surprise.

Key SLA elements to lock early (fields to confirm with buyer):
- Throughput unit: tokens/sec or requests/sec per model class (agree on tokenization/encoding).
- Commitment window: sustained baseline (e.g., 100k tokens/sec over 5 min rolling), plus burst bucket (e.g., 3x baseline for 60s)
- Concurrency and slotting: number of concurrent sessions supported with p95 latency target per session
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95 generation latency for canonical prompt size (specify sequence length)
- Availability: control-plane and data-plane availability (target % uptime, exclude scheduled maintenance windows)
- Isolation guarantee: dedicated inference pool + tenant isolation surface areas (compute, cache, network)
- Measurement and reporting cadence: daily usage export, hourly SLO rollups, monthly executive summary
- Credits & remedy: how much credit (% of invoice) for SLO misses and measurement methodology

Isolation — what we mean and how to describe it:
- Physical isolation: dedicated GPU nodes (no co-tenancy at the device level) or dedicated allocation slices on a cluster depending on buyer tolerance.
- Logical isolation: per-tenant model stores, KV caches, and encrypted ephemeral KV namespaces; strict access control for KMS/HSM integration.
- Network isolation: VPC peering or private link with customer-managed ingress/egress; optional air-gapped on-prem bundle for regulated customers.
- Operational isolation: separate logging/trace routing and rate-limit boundaries to prevent noisy neighbor escalation.

Measurement & instrumentation (how we will prove it):
- Primary metrics: tokens/sec, successful requests/sec, p95 response latencies for canonical prompt template, model-variant used, and cache hit rate
- Telemetry: per-route dashboards in Redwood Console with exportable CSVs; signed daily ingest for audit (S3/ELK delivery options)
- Arbitration: mutually agreed test harness (we own reference harness; buyer can run in their environment) and an on-demand replay window (last 14 days) for disputes
- Benchmarks: include baseline lab-run results (kernel selection, quantization profile used) as appendix in the final SOW

Pricing frameworks (commercial levers we typically use):
- Reserved base + overage: monthly reservation for baseline throughput + per-token/per-req unit for usage beyond baseline
- Burst smoothing: allow defined burst buckets at discounted overage to reduce denial during traffic spikes
- Performance credit model: precise credit calculation for missed SLOs (e.g., pro-rated % of monthly fee based on drop in delivered tokens/sec relative to commitment)
- Hybrid SKU: dedicated capacity + preferential hosted fallback (for unpredictable bursts where buyer prefers automatic fallback rather than throttling)
- Discount levers: longer commitments, larger baseline, and willingness to accept quantized model variants (low-precision) for cost reduction

Negotiation playbook & seller scripts (short):
- If buyer asks for 100% strict isolation and on-prem, respond: "We provide dedicated physical pools and an on-prem appliance option for regulated workloads; let's map the data flow and compliance controls you require — we can produce a boundary diagram and checklist."
- If buyer pushes to commoditize throughput as requests/sec only, respond: "Requests/sec hides variability from prompt length and model variant; we recommend token/sec commitments with a canonical prompt profile to make measurements reproducible."
- If procurement asks for unlimited burst for no extra fee: "We can support defined burst buckets; unlimited burst exposes all customers to capacity risk. We can offer a short-term promotional buffer as a concession for signed 12+ month commitments."

Buyer Q&A (common objections + suggested replies):
- "How do you measure a miss?" — "We use mutually-agreed telemetry: canonical prompt set, token counting rules, and an automated measurement suite. SLO rollups are visible in the Console and can be exported for audit."
- "What if we need more throughput mid-contract?" — "We offer immediate add-on capacity at predictable unit pricing and can schedule a one-time scale event; for guaranteed increases, we propose a 30-day ramp plan in the SOW."
- "How do you avoid noisy neighbors?" — "Dedicated pools remove co-tenancy at the device level; plus we enforce per-tenant concurrency limits and prefix/KV cache partitioning to stop cross-tenant interference."

Competitive callouts (how to differentiate in the field):
- Against managed cloud endpoints: emphasize transparent unit economics (token-level visibility), intelligent batching/caching that reduces cost, and a documented fallback policy for regional capacity issues.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize the operational burden saved (SRE runbooks, automatic kernel tuning, model rollout tooling) and our SLA-backed throughput guarantees.
- Against other inference providers: call out our unified API across hosted/dedicated/private — customers can start on hosted then move to dedicated without re-engineering their client code or metrics hooks.

Procurement-ready checklist (items to include in RFP/SOW):
- Definition of commitment: token/sec baseline, burst policy, measurement cadence
- Model & prompt canonicalization: list models in-scope, quantization profile, canonical prompt templates for latency measurement
- Isolation specifics: compute topology, KV/cache partitioning, network boundary, KMS/HSM requirements
- Monitoring & reporting: dashboard access, export format, SLA reporting cadence, contact list for incident escalation
- Remedies: credit formula, remediation windows, and termination rights for persistent SLA breaches
- Change management: process for capacity increases, model changes, and scheduled maintenance windows

Sample SLO credit clause (short, for procurement teams):
"If Redwood fails to deliver the committed baseline throughput as measured by the agreed telemetry for two consecutive 24-hour reporting periods, the customer will receive a service credit equal to X% of the monthly reserved fee for each day of non-compliance. Credits are limited to Y% per billing period."

Operational readiness (for SE to confirm before final offer):
- Confirm lab-run numbers for buyer's canonical prompt set and attach as Appendix A
- Validate availability of the requested region and GPU family for the contract start date
- Run quick-cost simulation: baseline reserved fees, expected overage, and 95th/99th percentile cost sensitivity for peak patterns
- Pre-authorize an on-call SRE and define runbook for first 90 days post-go-live

Field tips & friction areas we've seen:
- Procurement frequently pushes for ambiguous metrics ("throughput") — always bring the canonical prompt example and insist on token/sec or a well-defined proxy.
- Legal asks for unlimited culpability caps — sales should push for limited, tiered credits and remediation periods that align to predictable cost exposure.
- Buyers with strict compliance needs often want full on-prem; present a hybrid approach early (private control plane + dedicated pool) to avoid late-cycle surprises.

Appendix: quick reference snippets (for quoting in emails)
- "We commit to a baseline of N tokens/sec (canonical prompts) with a p95 latency target of T ms and a 3x burst buffer for short spikes. Measurement is via Redwood Console telemetry; credits apply per the SOW."
- "Isolation includes dedicated GPU pools, partitioned KV caches, VPC-level networking, and optional HSM-backed key management; we can diagram endpoints in 48 hours."

Next steps / action items for owner: 
- Draft Appendix A lab benchmark for Buyer X and attach kernel/quantization notes (owner: Marcus)
- Prepare a one-page bidder summary and a redlines-ready SOW template that includes the sample credit clause (owner: Priya)
- Sync with SRE to confirm capacity availability for requested start date (owner: Ethan)

Unresolved questions to surface in the deal war room:
- Acceptable maximum credit liability per month?
- Is buyer open to quantized model variants for a subset of traffic?
- Required retention period for audit-ready logs and telemetry?
